title: Extraction and analysis of liver lipids
author: Ryan Temel Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iy7cfzn

steps.title: Prepare tissue and internal standard
steps.instruction: Remove liver from the -80 °C freezer, place it into a cooler with liquid nitrogen, cut 50–100 mg of liver onto a glass plate to let adipose tissue thaw, chop with a razor blade keeping the tissue in one piece, add 100 mg 5‑α‑cholestane to a tared 16 × 100 mm glass screw‑top tube, dry any solvent under N₂ in a heating block, transfer the adipose tissue to the tube with a metal spatula (do not scrape the tube walls), weigh the tube plus tissue and record the wet weight.

substeps.instruction: Remove liver from -80 °C freezer and place into liquid‑nitrogen‑cooled cooler.
Place 50–100 mg liver onto a glass plate; allow adipose tissue to thaw.
Chop liver with a razor blade, keeping the tissue in one piece.
Place 100 mg 5‑α‑cholestane into a tared 16 × 100 mm glass screw‑top tube.
Dry off any solvent under N₂ in a heating block.
Transfer adipose tissue to the tube using a metal spatula (do not scrape tube walls).
Weigh tube + tissue and record wet weight.

steps.title: Extract lipids with chloroform‑methanol
steps.instruction: Add 3 ml 2:1 chloroform:methanol, dislodge tissue, incubate overnight at room temperature or at 55 °C for 1–2 h, centrifuge 1 500×g (2 700 rpm) at room temperature for 10 min, transfer the bottom lipid extract to a new 16 × 100 mm glass tube, wash the tissue residue with 2 ml 2:1 chloroform:methanol, centrifuge as before, combine wash with extract, and dry the combined extract under N₂ in a 55–60 °C heating block.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 ml 2:1 chloroform:methanol and dislodge tissue with a metal spatula.
Incubate overnight at room temperature or in a 55 °C heating block for 1–2 h.
Centrifuge 1 500×g (2 700 rpm) at room temperature for 10 min.
Transfer the bottom lipid extract to a new 16 × 100 mm glass screw‑top tube.
Wash the tissue residue with 2 ml 2:1 chloroform:methanol, centrifuge as above, and transfer the wash to the extract tube.
Dry the combined extract under N₂ in a 55–60 °C heating block.

steps.title: Acid‑catalyzed transesterification
steps.instruction: Add 6 ml 2:1 chloroform:methanol, vortex, place a 15 ml graduated tube to measure the bottom phase, add 1.2 ml 0.05 % H₂SO₄, cap and vortex vigorously, centrifuge 1 500×g (2 700 rpm) at room temperature for 10 min, record the bottom phase volume in the graduated tube, and aspirate the upper aqueous phase.

substeps.instruction: Add 6 ml 2:1 chloroform:methanol and vortex.
Insert a 15 ml glass graduated tube for bottom‑phase volume calculation.
Add 1.2 ml 0.05 % H₂SO₄, cap, and vortex vigorously.
Centrifuge 1 500×g (2 700 rpm) at room temperature for 10 min.
Record the bottom phase volume using the graduated tube.
Aspirate the upper aqueous phase.

steps.title: Prepare sample for GC analysis
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 ml of the bottom chloroform phase to a 16 × 100 mm glass tube, dry under liquid N₂ in a heating block, add 2 ml 95 % ethanol and 200 ml 50 % KOH, cap and incubate at ~60 °C for 3 h with periodic vortexing, add 2 ml hexane and vortex, add 2 ml water and vortex, centrifuge at 2 700 rpm at room temperature for 10 min, transfer the upper hexane layer to a clean 4 ml vial and dry under N₂, resuspend the residue in 250 µl hexane and transfer to a GC vial (dry before shipping if needed).

substeps.instruction: Transfer 1 ml bottom chloroform phase to a 16 × 100 mm glass screw‑top tube and dry under liquid N₂ in the heating block.
Add 2 ml 95 % ethanol and 200 ml 50 % KOH, cap, and incubate at ~60 °C for 3 h with periodic vortexing.
Add 2 ml hexane, vortex.
Add 2 ml water, vortex.
Centrifuge at 2 700 rpm at room temperature for 10 min.
Transfer the upper hexane phase to a clean 4 ml vial and dry under N₂.
Resuspend the dried extract in 250 µl hexane and transfer to a GC vial.
If samples are to be shipped, dry the extract completely before shipping.

steps.title: Prepare sample for enzymatic assays
steps.instruction: Using a glass volumetric pipet, transfer 1 ml of the bottom phase to a new 16 × 100 mm glass tube, add 2 ml 1 % Triton X‑100 dissolved in chloroform, dry under N₂ in a 55–60 °C heating block, add 1 ml water, cap, vortex, incubate at 55–60 °C for 10 min (vortex again at 5 min), centrifuge 1 500×g (2 700 rpm) at room temperature for 5 min, and if the supernatant is cloudy repeat with 0.5–0.25 ml bottom phase.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 1 ml bottom phase to a new 16 × 100 mm glass screw‑top tube with a glass volumetric pipet.
Add 2 ml 1 % Triton X‑100 in chloroform and dry under N₂ in a 55–60 °C heating block.
Add 1 ml water, cap, vortex, and place in the 55–60 °C heating block for 10 min; vortex again at the 5 min point.
Centrifuge 1 500×g (2 700 rpm) at room temperature for 5 min.
If the supernatant is clear, proceed to enzymatic assays; if cloudy, take 0.5–0.25 ml bottom phase and repeat steps a–d.

steps.title: Prepare Triton X‑100 standards
steps.instruction: Prepare lipid standards that contain Triton X‑100; ensure they are not plasma lipid standards.

steps.title: Total cholesterol enzymatic assay
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well plate, add 50 µl duplicate of each standard and sample, add 150 µl Pointe Scientific total cholesterol reagent, incubate at room temperature (or 37 °C if required) for 1 h, and read absorbance at 492 nm (or the reagent‑specified wavelength).

substeps.instruction: Plate 50 µl of each standard and sample in duplicate.
Add 150 µl total cholesterol reagent to each well.
Incubate at room temperature (or 37 °C) for 1 h.
Measure absorbance at 492 nm (or the appropriate wavelength).

steps.title: Free cholesterol enzymatic assay
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well plate, add 50 µl duplicate of each standard and sample, add 150 µl Free Cholesterol E (Wako) to each well, incubate at room temperature for 1 h, and read absorbance at 595 nm.

substeps.instruction: Plate 50 µl of each standard and sample in duplicate.
Add 150 µl Free Cholesterol E (Wako) to each well.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Measure absorbance at 595 nm.

steps.title: Triglyceride enzymatic assay
steps.instruction: In a 96‑well plate, add 50 µl duplicate of each standard, add 40 µl blank +10 µl sample in duplicate, add 150 µl L‑Type Triglycerides M reagent 1 (Wako) and incubate 10 min at room temperature, then add 50 µl L‑Type Triglycerides M reagent 2, incubate 1 h at room temperature, and read absorbance at 595 nm.

substeps.instruction: Plate 50 µl of each standard in duplicate.
Plate 40 µl blank + 10 µl sample in duplicate.
Add 150 µl L‑Type Triglycerides M reagent 1 (Wako) and incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Add 50 µl L‑Type Triglycerides M reagent 2, incubate 1 h at room temperature.
Measure absorbance at 595 nm.

steps.title: Protein quantification for normalization
steps.instruction: Place the uncapped tube containing extracted liver into a 100 °C oven for 20 min, add 4 ml 1 N NaOH, cap the tube, return to the 100 °C oven, vortex every 30 min until the liver is dissolved, and assay 5 µl lysate in duplicate using a Lowry protein assay.

substeps.instruction: Place uncapped tube with extracted liver in a 100 °C oven for 20 min.
Add 4 ml 1 N NaOH and cap the tube.
Return the capped tube to the 100 °C oven.
Vortex every 30 min until the liver is fully dissolved.
Assay 5 µl of the lysate in duplicate with a Lowry protein assay.
